Original:
afsos nabizadiyon ka shaam me jaana
sajjad se pucho
Translation:
Ask Sajjad about the tragedy
of the Prophet's granddaughters being taken to Sham.

Original:
sar nange woh maa behno ka darbar me jana
sajjad se pucho
Translation:
Ask Sajjad what it was like
for those mothers and sisters to enter the court with uncovered heads.

Original:
chupti thi nabizadi nabizadi ke peeche kis sharmo haya se
aur shimr ka un bibiyon ke naam bataana
sajjad se pucho
Translation:
Ask Sajjad how, out of modesty and shame,
one granddaughter of the Prophet hid behind another,
and how Shimr called out the names of those noble ladies.

Original:
baithe hue darbaar me sab chote bade the
sadaat khade the
sar tasht me rakkha hua zainab ko dikhana
sajjad se pucho
Translation:
Ask Sajjad how, while all—young and old—were seated in the court,
the family of the Prophet were made to stand,
and Zainab was shown her brother's head placed upon a tray.

Original:
jab dukhtare shabbir ne zinda me kaza ki
aafat ki ghadi thi
woh nanhi si mayyat bandhe hatho se uthana
sajjad se pucho
Translation:
Ask Sajjad about the dreadful moment
when the daughter of Shabbir passed away in the prison.
He had to lift her tiny body with his hands still bound.

Original:
jab ghusl sakina ko waha de chuki ghassala
tha sab ka bura haal
us nanhi si mayyat pe nishaan rassi ke paana
sajjad se pucho
Translation:
Ask Sajjad how, after Sakina's ritual washing had been completed,
everyone was overcome with grief,
and rope marks were found upon that little body.
